newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex chief says former racketeer has stake in Nomura.
newsitem.headline: Ex chief says former racketeer has stake in Nomura.

text.p: A racketeer linked to a payoff scandal at Nomura Securities Co Ltd is also a major shareholder in the company, the brokerage firm's ex-president said on Friday.
Hideo Sakamaki, who stepped down to take responsibility for the scandal, was testifying before a parliamentary committee looking into the affair.

Nomura has admitted that two directors made payments that were funnelled to "sokaiya" racketeers, who extort money from a company by threatening to disturb shareholder meetings. Japanese commercial law has prohibited paying off racketeers since 1982.
"The client has owned 300,000 shares (in Nomura) under corporate names since, I think, the beginning of 1989," Sakamaki said. He said the first shares were purchased in 1970.
Sakamaki, who in the past helped organise shareholders' meetings, said that he had never thought about making special arrangements to get along with racketeers.
Sakamaki said he believes only the two directors identified were involved in the payoffs, which came to light in March after an internal investigation by Nomura.

He also defended the company's system of having 8,000 to 9,000 special VIP accounts out of its total of five million customers, saying it does not provide preferential treatment at the expense of other clients.
He said that the accounts were for customers who needed careful treatment, including ones who complained about receiving direct mail. He said any clients can be classified as a VIP.

On the continuing probe by prosecutors and officials from Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), Sakamaki said that Nomura was fully cooperating with the investigators. Nomura will submit its client list to regulators if requested, he said.
